title: Projection compatibility for the tail of the graph composition word
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring and f:X→Y, g:Y→Z arbitrary scheme morphisms with supplied compactifications cf,cg,ch for f,g,f≫g. Let S and D:S.functor→Ff⋙Fg be the first graph presentation and its explicit tail comparison [def-sf-etale-graph-word-projection]. For every M in D(X_et,A) and K in D(Z_et,A), tensoring D_M with K, then applying the projection for cg and Fg applied to projection for cf, equals sfGraphWordProjection(S;M,K), followed by D at M tensor L(f≫g)*K, followed by FgFf applied to M tensor the canonical pullback compositor L(f≫g)*K→Lf*Lg*K. This is the projection square only for the remaining graph word e3 followed by inverse e2, and imposes no qc, Noetherianity or boundedness hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply the Cartesian graph-interchange projection square to the explicit graphDiagram(f,g,cg,ch). This square concerns only the proper/open interchange and its compositors, before comparing with cf or shrinking the first neighborhood.

Use the already proved graphCompositor_normalization and diagramCompIso_raw identities to identify sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso with B for the composite presentation, inverse raw interchange, and the inverse B for the source presentation. These are the same graph maps as in the original tail, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

Apply sfGraphCompactificationComparison_projection for cf and the source presentation, and for ch and the composite presentation. The categorical projection_interchange_transport helper pastes these two squares with the interchange square: postcompose by the source graph comparison and interchange, use their naturality, and cancel them. This gives the full graph-compositor projection square.

Use sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso_factor to factor the full graph compositor into the first graph comparison and sfGraphCompositionTailIso. Apply the graph-model projection square to ch and the first graph presentation and cancel tensoring the first comparison, which is an isomorphism. The remaining equality is exactly the unchanged tail projection statement.

lean.statement:
theorem sfGraphCompositionTailIso_projection
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (cf : Compactification f) (cg : Compactification g)
    (ch : Compactification (f ≫ g))
    (M : DerivedCategoryModule A X) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A Z) :
    ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) Z).map
        ((sfGraphCompositionTailIso A f g cf cg ch).hom.app M)).app K ≫
      sfCompactProjection A cg
        ((rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) cf).obj M) K ≫
      (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) cg).map
        (sfCompactProjection A cf M
          ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) g).leftDerivedFunctor.obj K)) =
    sfGraphWordProjection A (sfCompositionGraphPresentation f g cg ch) M K ≫
      (sfGraphCompositionTailIso A f g cf cg ch).hom.app
        (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj M).obj
          ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (f ≫ g)).leftDerivedFunctor.obj K)) ≫
      (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) cg).map
        ((rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) cf).map
          (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj M).map
            ((leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f g).hom.app K)))
